[engine] A bit-identical gate is only meaningful for a graph that is itself reproducible: before quoting 'candidate == reference' as a result, establish that the same arm, build and generation length reproduces one and the same digest over N rounds. For a run-to-run unstable arm the gate compares the candidate against one arbitrary sample of the reference, so a PASS is a coincidence and the gate has no discriminating power.

<!-- generated by harness_engine/build_memories.py from traces/lessons.jsonl -->
<!-- lesson_id: eng-gate-0007 | class: gate-integrity | superseded_by: - -->

**class**: `gate-integrity`

## 為什麼（because）

On this project the neutral-baseline arm p25-gputime is stable at every length (N=24 -> dc055e63 across every sweep and every rebuild; N=40 -> 3d8fa55f; N=100 -> 28097996), while the S1 arm p25-slotgpu under the segmented dispatcher produced THREE different digests in three rounds of one sweep on one build (29ca694a / 672585db / b8c705cc) at N=24, and produced eight further distinct values across the sweeps at other lengths. Under the non-segmented dispatcher the same arm collapses to a single stable ff68c5a2. So the same gate would be deterministic on one arm and a coin flip on the other, with no change to the gate. The failure mode is therefore silent in the direction that matters: the reference dump is a single sample, so an unstable candidate that happens to sample the reference value once reports PASS. Note also that three digests of the baseline arm that look like dispatcher sensitivity are actually generation-length effects -- md5 is only comparable within one build fingerprint AND one predicted_n, which is why the earlier 3d8fa55f/28097996 readings must not be attributed to the dispatcher.
